messages:
Iris (PM): Punting a short thread — idea: 'Surge Budget Lanes' (SBL). Blend of per-route prepaid credits + optional reserved mini-slots. Goal: let customers buy predictable short-term capacity per-route without full Dedicated commits. Thoughts on scope & launch gates?

Tobias (Eng): Two feature toggles: soft-lane (probabilistic priority) and hard-lane (short reserved slots tied to credits). Hard-lane is more expensive infra-wise because we need short-term reservation + isolation. Soft-lane is cheaper but less deterministic.

Mina (DevEx): Console & API needs: attach SBL to a route, pick mode (soft|hard), set window length and cap, preview estimated coverage (requests/min covered). Also show credit history and alerts for low balance. Minimal pilot UI: route dropdown + attach panel + event feed.

Ken (Sales): Sales framing: "route-level surge budget". Customers want simple use-cases: deploy protection, campaign bursts, checkout spikes. Pilot offer: 3 free surge windows (soft) or one discounted hard-window for enterprise trials.

Luca (Finance): Pricing models to consider: time-based windows (e.g., 1-hour hard slot), credit buckets (X requests per credit), or hybrid. Need mapping to unit cost: how many credits = 1 GPU-second equivalent? Also flag revenue recognition for pre-buys.

Anya (Legal): Legal redlines: do not market soft-lane as an SLA. Hard-lane can carry an SLA if explicitly reserved and priced. Require explicit customer consent for traffic steering to fallbacks. Add misuse and rollback clauses.

Iris (PM): Proposed pilot scope: implement soft-lane first (cheaper, fewer infra changes), include route attach, scheduling, visibility, and billing telemetry. Pilot with 3 customers across SMB and mid-market. Success metrics: measurable drop in 95th latency for attached routes during spikes; platform cost delta <6% at 99th; positive pilot CSAT.

Tobias (Eng): Feasibility: soft-lane needs quick O(1) check at ingress and weight adjustments in scheduler + tagging for metrics. Estimate 2 sprints to MVP if we reuse routing hooks. Hard-lane adds reservation allocator and eviction policies — mostly separate runbook.

Mina (DevEx): Console UX caveats: show expected credit consumption for example spike patterns; allow scheduling recurring windows (e.g., every Fri deploy); add an "emergency apply" button with confirmation. I'll mock flows this week.

Ken (Sales): SKU sketch for discussion (soft-lane):
```
sku_id: SBL-SOFT-200
name: "Surge Budget Lane - Soft (200 credits)"
units: credits
bundle: 200
price_usd: 129
validity_days: 30
notes: "probabilistic priority; no guaranteed SLA; per-route attach"
```

Luca (Finance): Quick margin ask: what's the expected infra delta for a typical spike that uses 200 credits? We need a conservative cost-per-credit to validate pricing. Also propose PAYG fallback price for ad-hoc top-ups.

Anya (Legal): Pilot T&Cs: explicit opt-in, clear no-SLA language for soft-lane, audit logging requirement, and a rollback/kill-switch clause. For hard-lane pilots we need an explicit reservation contract and SLA appendix.

Tobias (Eng): Ops ask: run two sims: (A) 5min 6x spike on a single route with soft-lane attached (200 credits). (B) 1min high burst to test emergency apply. Capture: credit burn, 95/99 latency delta, and cluster CPU/GPU impact. @sim-bot can you queue both?

sim-bot: Queued simulations: #13001 (SBL soft 5min 6x spike, 200 credits) and #13002 (SBL emergency 1min burst). ETA ~3h. Results will be posted back to this thread.

Mina (DevEx): Also need an example REST API for pilots. Draft proposal: POST /v1/routes/{route_id}/surge-attach { sku: SBL-SOFT-200, mode: soft, auto_apply: [deploys], schedule: null }

Iris (PM): Next steps: Tobias -> tech spec + runtime safety (kill-switch); Mina -> console mock + API example; Anya -> pilot T&Cs; Ken -> shortlist 3 pilot customers; Luca -> initial cost-per-credit model. I'll gather into PRD draft and share EOD Friday. Thanks :rocket:
